title: Chernobyl
creator: Craig Mazin
awards: Won 10 Primetime Emmys. 87 wins & 60 nominations total
tagline: What is the cost of lies?
plot: In April 1986, the city of Chernobyl in the Soviet Union suffers one of the worst nuclear disasters in the history of mankind. Consequently, many heroes put their lives on the line in the following days, weeks and months.
plotsummary:
In April 1986, the city of Chernobyl in the Soviet Union suffers one of the worst nuclear disasters in the history of mankind. Consequently, many heroes put their lives on the line in the following days, weeks and months.

In April 1986, a huge explosion erupted at the Chernobyl nuclear power station in northern Ukraine. This series follows the stories of the men and women, who tried to contain the disaster, as well as those who gave their lives preventing a subsequent and worse one.

On 26 April 1986 the Number 4 reactor at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine exploded and caught fire. This is the story of that event, the aftermath, how the real reasons for the incident were covered up and how one man fought to reveal them.

On April 26, 1986 the Chernobyl nuclear power plant near Pripyat, Ukraine experienced a malfunction which resulted in a core explosion in reactor 4. This miniseries follows Valery Legasov, the lead scientist working to control the disaster, Boris Shcherbina, a Soviet politician representing the interests of the Soviet government during the disaster, and Ulana Khomyuk, a nuclear physicist working to uncover the truth about what really happened at Chernobyl. This series tackles the problems that arise when the truth is ignored and kept from the public, begging the question: "What is the cost of lies?".

In 1986, Chernobyl suffered the worst nuclear meltdown in human history: changing the course of the Soviet Union and leading to the inevitable downfall of Communism in Europe. This is the story of what happened on the frontlines of the chaos, the cover-ups behind closed doors, and the civilians held prisoner to the circumstances of Earth's greatest nuclear disaster.

On 26th April 1986, Reactor Number Four at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Soviet Ukraine explodes during a routine safety test, triggering the worst nuclear disaster in human history. In the immediate aftermath, plant workers and the first wave of firefighters are sent in with no understanding of the true danger they face, absorbing lethal doses of radiation while Soviet officials scramble to contain both the disaster and the information surrounding it.

Soviet nuclear physicist Valery Legasov is appointed to lead the scientific response to the disaster alongside Soviet Deputy Prime Minister Boris Shcherbina, a loyal party bureaucrat who initially prioritises political optics over human life. As the two men are forced to work together, Shcherbina gradually comes to understand the catastrophic scale of what has happened, and the pair form an unlikely partnership built on mutual respect and a shared determination to prevent an even greater catastrophe.

As the true cause of the explosion becomes clearer, Legasov and his colleagues face obstruction at every level of the Soviet system. Officials suppress information, falsify reports, and prioritise the reputation of the Communist Party over the safety of millions. Meanwhile, hundreds of thousands of liquidators - soldiers, miners, and civilians - are mobilised to contain the disaster, many of them given little to no protective equipment and sent on missions they are not told will likely kill them. The series unflinchingly depicts the human cost of these decisions, following individual workers, plant operators, and local residents whose lives are destroyed by both the explosion and the cover-up that follows.

Nuclear physicist Ulana Khomyuk conducts her own independent investigation into the true cause of the explosion, uncovering a catastrophic design flaw in the RBMK reactor - a flaw that Soviet authorities had known about and deliberately concealed for years. Her findings become central to the trial of the plant's senior officials.

The series culminates in the trial of plant director Viktor Bryukhanov, chief engineer Nikolai Fomin, and deputy chief engineer Anatoly Dyatlov, where Legasov delivers a devastating testimony that publicly exposes the truth about the reactor's fatal design flaw and the systemic lies that allowed it to remain hidden. In doing so, he effectively ends his own career and seals his fate within the Soviet establishment. The final episode reveals that Legasov died by suicide two years after the disaster, on the second anniversary of the explosion, having recorded a series of tapes detailing the full truth - tapes that open the series and frame the entire story.
